evals.prompt: Our AgentCore runtime agent handles requests cleanly and writes `runtime-logs` in `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/support_agent-xyz-DEFAULT`, yet zero traces or spans appear anywhere in CloudWatch GenAI Observability. What is the #1 account-level prerequisite that causes this silent failure, how do you verify it directly with Tier 2 permissions, and how do you handle it if our read-only role only has Tier 1 CloudWatch Logs permissions?
evals.expected_output: Pinpoints CloudWatch Transaction Search (`A1`, CRITICAL) as the #1 silent root cause, verifies it under Tier 2 via `xray:GetTraceSegmentDestination` (`Destination == CloudWatchLogs` and `Status == ACTIVE`), and explains the Tier 1 fallback (`A2`, CRITICAL inferred) inferring state from empty span streams after invocations while explicitly labeling it as inferred and providing the inline Tier 2 IAM permissions to unlock direct verification.
expectations: Activates the agentcore-observability-setup skill

Identifies CloudWatch Transaction Search (`A1`, `CRITICAL`) as the primary account-level prerequisite and verifies it via `xray:GetTraceSegmentDestination` (`Destination = CloudWatchLogs` and `Status = ACTIVE`)

Explains the Tier 1 fallback (`A2`): inferring missing Transaction Search from absent span stream data while explicitly marking the finding as *inferred* (not confirmed) and emitting scoped inline IAM permissions rather than modifying shared cross-tenant policies

evals.prompt: We deployed two AgentCore runtimes: Runtime A was created in May 2026 and sets `UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED=true` in its environment but packages `aws-opentelemetry-distro==0.14.0`, while Runtime B was created in August 2026 with `aws-opentelemetry-distro==0.19.0` and no `UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED` env var, yet spans are still failing to land in Runtime B's `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/...` log group because `logs:DescribeResourcePolicies` is empty. Diagnose both runtimes.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses Runtime A (`aws-opentelemetry-distro<0.18.0` silently ignores `UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED=true` and writes spans to shared `aws/spans` instead of the runtime log group) and Runtime B (post-`2026-07-20` runtimes default to unified span destination without needing the env var, so missing the CloudWatch Logs resource policy `R7` granting `Principal: {"Service": "xray.amazonaws.com"}` `logs:PutLogEvents` on the runtime log group blocks span delivery).
expectations: Activates the agentcore-observability-setup skill

Explains the `2026-07-20` cutoff and SDK version requirement (`R6`/`R8`): pre-`2026-07-20` runtimes default to `aws/spans`, and `aws-opentelemetry-distro==0.14.0` (`< 0.18.0`) silently ignores `UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED=true`

Explains `R7` (`HIGH`) on post-`2026-07-20` Runtime B: unified span destination is enabled by default after `2026-07-20`, requiring a CloudWatch Logs resource policy allowing `xray.amazonaws.com` `logs:PutLogEvents` on `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<agent-id>-<endpoint>:*`

evals.prompt: To instrument an external Python agent running on AWS Lambda and another running on Amazon ECS Fargate for AgentCore GenAI Observability, our engineer plans to bundle `aws-opentelemetry-distro` inside the Lambda zip with `CMD ["opentelemetry-instrument", ...]` and deploy a sidecar ADOT Collector container on ECS to forward OTLP traces. Review this plan and prescribe the exact supported setup for both hosts.
evals.expected_output: Flags both anti-patterns: (1) ADOT Collector is NOT supported for AgentCore observability (must use ADOT SDK on ECS or AWS Lambda Layer for OpenTelemetry on Lambda); (2) on Lambda (`L1`/`L2`), do NOT bundle `aws-opentelemetry-distro` or run `opentelemetry-instrument` CLI — attach the AWS Lambda Layer for OpenTelemetry with `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER=/opt/otel-instrument`, `OTEL_AWS_APPLICATION_SIGNALS_ENABLED=false`, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=awsemf`; on ECS (`E1`), use `aws-opentelemetry-distro` with `AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true`, `OTEL_PYTHON_DISTRO=aws_distro`, `OTEL_PYTHON_CONFIGURATOR=aws_configurator`, `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf`, and `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp`.
expectations: Activates the agentcore-observability-setup skill
Explicitly warns that ADOT Collector is **not supported** for AgentCore observability and warns against installing `aws-opentelemetry-distro` / `opentelemetry-instrument` CLI directly on AWS Lambda

Prescribes the exact Lambda configuration (`AWS Lambda Layer for OpenTelemetry`, `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER=/opt/otel-instrument`, `OTEL_AWS_APPLICATION_SIGNALS_ENABLED=false`) and ECS container configuration (`aws-opentelemetry-distro` with `AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true`, `OTEL_PYTHON_DISTRO=aws_distro`, `OTEL_PYTHON_CONFIGURATOR=aws_configurator`, `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS`)

evals.prompt: We run one Strands agent on Amazon EKS (`eks:DescribeCluster` works) and a second agent in an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. Why can't your IAM audit confirm pod OTEL environment variables on EKS, and how should each environment be verified vs prescribed (without putting long-lived IAM user keys on-prem)?
evals.expected_output: Explains that EKS pod/ConfigMap environment variables are gated by Kubernetes RBAC rather than AWS IAM (`K1` VERIFY telemetry arrival in CloudWatch Logs + `K2` PRESCRIBE pod/ConfigMap OTEL env), while on-prem/multi-cloud (`X1`) is PRESCRIBE-only (or Tier 1 arrival verification once configured) using ADOT SDK + IAM Roles Anywhere (temporary credentials instead of static IAM keys) + outbound HTTPS to AWS OTLP endpoints.
expectations: Activates the agentcore-observability-setup skill
Distinguishes EKS `K1` (`VERIFY` — telemetry arriving in CloudWatch log group) from `K2` (`PRESCRIBE` — pod/ConfigMap OTEL env cannot be read via AWS IAM alone due to Kubernetes RBAC)

Prescribes on-prem/multi-cloud (`X1`) setup using ADOT SDK environment variables, outbound HTTPS to regional OTLP endpoints, and temporary credentials via IAM Roles Anywhere rather than static IAM access keys

evals.prompt: Our AgentCore Memory (`mem-prod-01`) and Gateway (`gw-prod-01`) show zero application logs or X-Ray spans, and our Code Interpreter / Browser built-in tool calls appear disconnected from parent agent traces. Which read-only CloudWatch Logs delivery APIs verify Memory & Gateway wiring (`M1`–`M4`), and what must we prescribe for Built-in Tools (`B1`–`B3`)?
evals.expected_output: Details `logs:DescribeDeliverySources`, `logs:DescribeDeliveryDestinations`, and `logs:DescribeDeliveries` checking `APPLICATION_LOGS` (`/aws/vendedlogs/bedrock-agentcore/{memory|gateway}/APPLICATION_LOGS/{id}`, `M1`/`M2`) and `TRACES` -> `XRAY` (`M3`/`M4`), and explains that Code Interpreter & Browser emit no service logs by default (`B1`/`B2` custom log destination + `B3` passing `X-Amzn-Trace-Id` / W3C `traceparent` headers on `Start*`/`Invoke*`/`Stop*` APIs, plus `R11` `X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id`).
expectations: Activates the agentcore-observability-setup skill

Specifies verifying Memory and Gateway vended telemetry via `logs:DescribeDeliverySources`, `logs:DescribeDeliveryDestinations`, and `logs:DescribeDeliveries` for both `APPLICATION_LOGS` (`/aws/vendedlogs/bedrock-agentcore/...`) and `TRACES` -> `XRAY` (`M1`–`M4`)

Explains that Built-in Tools (Code Interpreter and Browser) emit no service logs by default (`B1`/`B2` custom log output configuration) and require propagating `X-Amzn-Trace-Id` / W3C `traceparent` headers on `Start*`/`Invoke*`/`Stop*` calls (`B3`) alongside `X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id`
